stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C funding round, valuing the company at $1.6 billion. This investment underscores the increasing demand for co-orbital security solutions, particularly from the DoD. With defense budgets tightening, companies like True Anomaly are positioning themselves as essential players in the national security landscape.
stories.soWhat: In a world where threats are more nuanced, True Anomaly's funding suggests that investors are betting on space as the next frontier of defense.

stories.head: Vast signs partners for commercial space station
stories.body: Vast has added several new partners to its commercial space station initiative, focusing on microgravity research. This collaboration trend highlights a shift in how private companies approach space entrepreneurship, moving towards shared resources and expertise. The exact financial terms remain undisclosed, but the strategic partnerships indicate a growing confidence in commercial space operations.
stories.soWhat: If collaboration is the new black, then Vast just opened a trendy boutique—expect more players to jump on the bandwagon.

stories.head: Vantor selects BAE for next-gen imaging satellites
stories.body: Vantor has chosen BAE Systems to develop its next-generation imaging satellites, marking a significant commitment to high-resolution capabilities. While the contract value hasn't been disclosed, this partnership is indicative of BAE's robust position in the defense supply chain. With imaging satellites becoming increasingly critical for both commercial and military applications, this move solidifies BAE's foothold in the sector.
stories.soWhat: The imaging game is heating up, and BAE's involvement suggests they might be the ones to watch as demand for clarity in space grows.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's next moves
watchlist.body: With fresh funding in hand, True Anomaly's strategy will be pivotal in shaping the co-orbital security market.

watchlist.title: Vast's partnerships could reshape commercial space
watchlist.body: As Vast continues to onboard partners, its approach could set a precedent for future commercial space ventures.

watchlist.title: BAE's imaging satellites may attract more contracts
watchlist.body: The success of Vantor's project could lead to additional contracts for BAE in the imaging satellite domain.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
